highlights.title: A runaway command can't take kwant down
highlights.text: On Linux, when a bot's command or AI CLI uses up the memory, the system now stops it, not kwant. kwant keeps running and says what happened.

highlights.title: A stopped command says why
highlights.text: When the system stops a command or the claude, codex or grok CLI, kwant says so in plain words: memory ran out, or something outside stopped it.

highlights.title: Your reason for Deny shows in Details
highlights.text: When you deny a step and say why, Details show your words under "You said no; nothing ran", so you can see later why it didn't run.

fixes: On a narrow phone, Deny and Always allow keep each label on one line.
Get started now opens at its top, not scrolled to the bottom.
Someone new to kwant no longer sees a "moved" notice about a change they never saw, and Approvals marks Ask only when risky as the default.
